documentation.title: Per-point history carried across a re-cut mortar partition
documentation.description:
initialGapHandling="zero" together with slidingType="large" and segmentation="mortar" used to be REJECTED with an error, because re-cutting the mortar partition replaces the contact integration points and the frozen as-meshed gap lives on a point. This testcase is that combination working.
HOW IT WAS MADE TO WORK. Not by a transfer operator bolted onto a per-iteration re-cut, but by observing that the point set never had to be stable across the whole analysis -- only within one Newton solve. Both history quantities already advance ONLY between solves, which is what makes the Uzawa update and the friction return map well-defined functions of u. So the partition is held FIXED for the duration of each solve and re-cut at the step boundary, where the stored field is interpolated onto the new points. The PAIRING is untouched and still follows the body every iteration.
WHAT MAKES THE HISTORY VISIBLE. The block's bottom edge is meshed as a WEDGE above a flat primary surface, and initialGapHandling="zero" freezes it and subtracts it from every later gap. The wedge is 140 times the elastic deflection, so a point that lost its offset on a re-cut would find an open gap, drop out of the active set and dump its load on its neighbours. That is why numActivePoints is the assertion and not a tolerance: the failure mode is discrete.
The block is driven u_x = t^2 over five steps, misaligned with the primary grid at every intermediate step, so there are five re-cuts and five history transfers. u_x = t^2 rather than t so the drive starts from zero VELOCITY; a linear ramp is a velocity step at t = 0, which rings the block. Transient rather than a chain of static sequence steps, because the step boundary has to be the boundary of a SOLVE with the contact interface living across it -- each sequenceStep would build its own interfaces, so the history would be re-initialised and the testcase would pass while testing nothing.
WHAT IT ASSERTS
1. contactForceY = 1e6, the vertical equilibrium of the block, exact at every step. 2. numActivePoints = 12, every contact point still in contact after five re-cuts. Control: the same model with initialGapHandling="fromMesh" -- what a total loss of the offsets looks like -- ends with numActivePoints = 0 and contactForceY = 0. The block falls off the wedge, so the offsets are not a refinement here, they are what holds the model up. 3. The partition fingerprints numCells / numPoints, and integratedArea, which must NOT move. 4. Agreement with the segmentation="gpts" run, which has no partition and never transfers anything: the resultant agrees exactly while minGap differs, being a pointwise extremum on two different point sets.
The counts describe the partition the last solve was integrated on, i.e. cut at the END of the previous step. The transfer is a weighted least-squares fit of a linear polynomial, so it reproduces this particular (linear) field exactly -- deliberately, so the testcase is a statement about the plumbing rather than about interpolation quality.
